english.title: Leave / place a vehicle / bicycle / conveyance on Transport for London road transport premises causing obstruction
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) while in charge of a

(A)_[motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY THE VEHICLE..),]_
(B)_[bicycle,]_
(C)_[a conveyance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CONVEYANCE..),]_

left or placed it on Transport for London road transport premises at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), in a manner or place where it might have caused an obstruction or hindrance to the operator or any person using the premises
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 11(3)(i) and 14 of the Transport for London Road Transport Premises Byelaws made under paragraph 26 of Schedule 11 to the Greater London Authority Act 1999 and confirmed under section 67 of the Transport Act 1962.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Byelaw 13 for the provision of a name and address by persons suspected of breaching this byelaw.
(ii) See byelaw 15 for a power to remove persons breaching this byelaw
(iii) See byelaw 16 for the requirement for authorised persons exercising any power conferred any of the Byelaws to produce a form of identification when requested to do so.
(iv) See Byelaw 17 in relation to the provision of notices.
(v) Byelaw 11(4) provides that any vehicle, bicycle or other conveyance used, left or placed in breach of Byelaw 11(3) may be removed and/or stored by or under the direction of the Operator or authorised person.
(vi) Byelaw 11(5) provides that the owner of any vehicle, bicycle or other conveyance shall be liable to the Operator or authorised person for the costs incurred in removing and storing it in addition to any penalty for the breach of Byelaw 11.
